newsitem.title: USA: OLYMPICS-JAPAN GAMES PRESENT FOOD CHALLENGE: U.S. SKI OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-JAPAN GAMES PRESENT FOOD CHALLENGE: U.S. SKI OFFICIAL.

text.p: The head of the U.S. Ski and Snowboard Association said Wednesday the 1998 Winter Olympics in Japan will present a special challenge to U.S. athletes and coaches: the food.
"The traditional Japanese diet is more fish-oriented than what Americans are used to," said USSA chief Bill Marolt.
"It's not whether we're right and they're wrong, or vice versa, but it's definitely something else we have to take into consideration."
He added: "I like fish but I'm not so sure three weeks of meals so heavy in fish and seafood would go over well with our athletes."

Marolt had an ulterior motive for the observation, announcing a U.S. Ski and Snowboard Association "partnership" with Healthy Choice foods to draw up nutritional plans for the 12 teams in seven sports governed by the USSA.

Mounds of crushed ice and bogus flakes from snow-blowing machines around Wollman Rink in New York City's Central Park provided lunchtime park visitors with a midwinter motif in midsummer as nine U.S. skiers including 1994 Olympic downhill gold medallist Tommy Moe showed off various skiing skills.
